props.gloss_en: in a garden bed six by six handbreadths one may sow five kinds of seed, four on the bed's four sides and one in the middle
as it is said, 'for as the earth brings forth its growth and as a garden causes its seeds to grow' (Isa 61:11) -- not 'its seed' but 'its seeds'
Rav Yehuda: 'brings forth' one, 'its growth' one -- two; 'its seeds' two -- four; 'causes to grow' one -- five
the Sages hold as established that five [kinds] in six [handbreadths] do not draw sustenance from one another
R' Yochanan: what is written 'do not move your neighbour's border which the first ones set' (Deut 19:14) -- a border the first ones set, do not move

R' Yonatan: 'these are the sons of Seir the Chori, the inhabitants of the land' (Gen 36:20) -- is everyone else an inhabitant of the sky? rather, they were expert in the settlement of the land, saying: this rod's length for olives, this for vines, this for figs
R' Yonatan: and 'Chori' -- for they smelled the earth
Rav Pappa: and 'Chivi' -- for they tasted the earth like a snake
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: 'Chori' -- for they became free of their possessions
Rav Asi: the [mishna's] bed -- its interior is six, besides its borders
the baraita: a bed -- its interior is six
R' Yehuda: the [border's] width is the full width of a foot
R' Zeira: R' Yehuda's reason -- 'and you water with your foot like a garden of herbs' (Deut 11:10): as a foot is a handbreadth, so a border is a handbreadth
Rav: [the mishna's] bed -- we learned it of a bed in a ruin
בי רב in Rav's name: [the mishna speaks] where he fills the corners
a decree, lest he fill the corners
if a vegetable rosh tor [a tapering point] entered another field, it is permitted, because the end of the field is visible
Shmuel: we learned [the mishna] of a bed among beds
Rav Sheshet: where one cut a single furrow across its whole [length], the mixing comes and nullifies the row
Rav Asi: its mixing does not nullify the row
one who plants two rows of cucumbers, two of gourds, two of Egyptian beans -- permitted; one row of cucumbers, one of gourds, one of Egyptian beans -- forbidden
R' Yochanan: one who wishes to fill his whole garden with vegetables makes a bed six by six, draws five circles in it, and fills its corners with whatever he wishes
Rav Ashi: if they were sown lengthwise he sows them widthwise; widthwise -- he sows them lengthwise
the work-space of a vegetable beside another vegetable is six handbreadths, and one views them as a square board
